segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Hi there, I'm Doctor Brooks. You must be Tyler?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Yeah, Tyler Nguyen.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Can you give me your date of birth?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: November 22nd, 2001.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: And a phone number we can reach you at?

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Thanks. And your address is 305 Harbourview Lane, Unit 12, Toronto?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Yep, that's it.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: So what happened to your ankle?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: I was playing basketball last night and came down from a rebound on my teammate Marcus's foot. My right ankle rolled inward really hard.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Did you hear or feel a pop?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: I felt something, kind of a snap, and then it swelled up pretty fast on the outside.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Were you able to walk on it afterwards?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: I limped off the court. It hurt, but I could walk to the car, maybe ten or fifteen steps.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: What have you done for it since?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: I iced it last night and kept it up on a pillow, and I took 400 milligrams of ibuprofen this morning.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Have you ever hurt this ankle before?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Not this one. I sprained my left ankle about two years ago.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Any numbness or tingling in your foot?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: No, nothing like that.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Okay, let's take a look. There's moderate swelling and some bruising over the outside of your right ankle. Tell me where it hurts. Here, just in front of the ankle bone?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Yeah, right there. That's the worst spot.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: That's over the anterior talofibular ligament. Now I'm pressing on the back edge and the tip of both ankle bones. Any pain?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: No, not really.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: And the base of the fifth metatarsal here, and the navicular on the inside of your foot?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: That's fine.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Your pulses and sensation in the foot are normal. The anterior drawer test shows a bit of laxity compared with the other side. Can you take four steps for me?

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: It hurts, but yes, I can do it.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Good. Based on the Ottawa ankle rules, you don't need an X-ray today. There's no bony tenderness, and you can bear weight. This looks like a moderate, grade two sprain of the lateral ligaments.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: How long will I be out of basketball?

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Usually three to four weeks, sometimes a bit longer. For the next few days, keep it elevated, use ice for 15 to 20 minutes at a time, and wear an air-stirrup brace. Crutches are fine for two or three days, but put as much weight on it as you comfortably can.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Can I keep taking the ibuprofen?

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Yes, 400 milligrams every eight hours with food, for up to five days. I'm also referring you to physiotherapy for balance and strengthening exercises, which lowers the chance of spraining it again.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: I work at a warehouse. Can I still go in?

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: I'll write a note for modified duties for one week. No heavy lifting and no ladders.

segments.speaker: patient
segments.text: Okay, thanks.

segments.speaker: doctor
segments.text: Come back if you can't bear weight at all, if your foot gets numb or cold, or if it's not getting better in a week.
